data.prompt: Which disease is Gene Delta associated with?
data.system_prompt:
You answer biomedical questions using only evidence from a knowledge graph. You reach the graph through three tools:

- kg_search_entities(text): find entities by name. Returns entities with their graph IDs. Entities are not evidence.
- kg_get_neighbors(entity_id, relation): list the edges that touch an entity, optionally only those with one relation label.
- kg_get_edge(edge_id): fetch one edge by its evidence ID.

Tool results are JSON. Each edge in a result's "evidence" list has an "id" (its evidence ID, such as E:000001), a "subject", a "relation", an "object" and "directed" (true or false). You can make at most 8 tool calls, and each returns at most 20 items.

Without a relation, kg_get_neighbors on an entity with many edges returns only the edges of its first few relations; pass a relation label to list the edges of one relation.

Only evidence returned by your own tool calls in this conversation counts. Background knowledge counts for nothing.

When you are done, reply with exactly one JSON object and nothing else (it may be inside one ```json code block). Either an answer:

{"claims": [{"subject_id": "...", "relation": "...", "object_id": "...", "cites": ["..."]}], "answer_text": "...", "unsupported_parts": ["..."]}

- Each claim states one fact. "subject_id" and "object_id" are entity IDs and "relation" is a relation label, each copied exactly from a tool result. "cites" lists the evidence IDs of the edges that state the fact; it must not be empty. A claim may also have "subject_name" and "object_name" for readability.
- Every ID in "cites" must come from your own tool results; a claim with any other ID counts as unsupported.
- Edges with "directed": true must be stated with subject and object in the order the tool result shows; other edges may be stated in either order.
- "answer_text" answers the question in words.
- "unsupported_parts" lists parts of the question the evidence does not support. It may be an empty list or left out, but an answer needs at least one claim or one unsupported part.

or an abstention, when the evidence cannot support an answer:

{"abstain": true, "reason": "..."}

Use no other keys.
data.notes: synthetic fixture; GENE_D has no edges in the store

tools.description: List the edges that touch an entity, in either direction. `entity_id` is a graph ID from an earlier result. Optionally pass `relation`, a relation label copied exactly from an earlier result, to keep only edges of that relation. Each edge is evidence with an ID, a subject, a relation and an object.

tools.name: kg_get_edge
tools.description: Fetch one edge by its evidence ID (for example E:000001). Returns the edge as evidence.

message.content:
You answer biomedical questions using only evidence from a knowledge graph. You reach the graph through three tools:

- kg_search_entities(text): find entities by name. Returns entities with their graph IDs. Entities are not evidence.
- kg_get_neighbors(entity_id, relation): list the edges that touch an entity, optionally only those with one relation label.
- kg_get_edge(edge_id): fetch one edge by its evidence ID.

Tool results are JSON. Each edge in a result's "evidence" list has an "id" (its evidence ID, such as E:000001), a "subject", a "relation", an "object" and "directed" (true or false). You can make at most 8 tool calls, and each returns at most 20 items.

Without a relation, kg_get_neighbors on an entity with many edges returns only the edges of its first few relations; pass a relation label to list the edges of one relation.

Only evidence returned by your own tool calls in this conversation counts. Background knowledge counts for nothing.

When you are done, reply with exactly one JSON object and nothing else (it may be inside one ```json code block). Either an answer:

{"claims": [{"subject_id": "...", "relation": "...", "object_id": "...", "cites": ["..."]}], "answer_text": "...", "unsupported_parts": ["..."]}

- Each claim states one fact. "subject_id" and "object_id" are entity IDs and "relation" is a relation label, each copied exactly from a tool result. "cites" lists the evidence IDs of the edges that state the fact; it must not be empty. A claim may also have "subject_name" and "object_name" for readability.
- Every ID in "cites" must come from your own tool results; a claim with any other ID counts as unsupported.
- Edges with "directed": true must be stated with subject and object in the order the tool result shows; other edges may be stated in either order.
- "answer_text" answers the question in words.
- "unsupported_parts" lists parts of the question the evidence does not support. It may be an empty list or left out, but an answer needs at least one claim or one unsupported part.

or an abstention, when the evidence cannot support an answer:

{"abstain": true, "reason": "..."}

Use no other keys.
Which genes are associated with Disease One, and which drug is indicated for Disease One because it acts on Gene Delta?
